title: 10 chips vs 100, 10,000 players. Fair coin: 866 broke the house. 49% coin: 64.
description:
Gambler's ruin. Each player starts with 10 chips against a house with 100, one chip a flip, until one side has nothing. Ten thousand games are played in each panel from seed 0 (numpy RandomState) on the same uniform draws: flip j of game i uses the same draw in both panels, and the player wins that flip when the draw is below p. The fair panel uses p = 0.50, the tilted panel p = 0.49, so exactly the draws in [0.49, 0.50) come out differently: 1.00% of them.

Measured at seed 0:
- fair coin: 866 of 10,000 players broke the house (8.66%; exact 10/110 = 9.09%, one standard deviation 0.29 points), 9,134 went bust; average game 950 flips (exact 1,000), median 212, longest 19,994; 3,281 games were over within 100 flips, 7,625 within 1,000
- 49% coin: 64 broke the house (0.64%; exact 0.61%), 9,936 went bust; average game 462 flips (exact 466), median 148, longest 14,488; 3,964 games over within 100 flips
- 13.5 times fewer winners with the tilted coin; on the same draws every tilted win is also a fair win (64 won in both panels, 802 won only with the fair coin, 0 only with the tilted coin)
- exact win probability from 10 against 100 for other coins: 49.5%: 2.76%, 48%: 0.02%, 45%: 0.00%
- independent check with 100,000 games per panel at seed 1: 9.15% and 0.61% broke the house, average games 1,004 and 467 flips

Why: with a fair coin the chance of reaching 110 before 0 is just 10/110. Any tilt compounds over the hundreds of flips a game lasts: with p = 0.49 the ratio 0.51/0.49 raised to the 100 chips the player must gain makes the climb about fifteen times less likely.

The numbers in the narration are the printed outputs of this exact run.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
